text:
elaine: Heads-up — ACME says a service token they just granted to a user for project 'acme-pay' is getting 403s in the console and API even though the console shows the user as a 'Project Developer'.

mike: Ack. Do we have a repro token or steps from the customer?

elaine: They sent a repro curl using the service token: 
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/acme-pay/models
```
Response was: {"error":"permission_denied","status":403,"detail":"missing scope:projects.read"}

jonathan: That error string looks like token scopes didn't get the project membership attached. Did they create the token before the role assign?

elaine: They created token after role assignment. They also said they used SCIM group sync to add the user to the project role (project-developers group).

mike: Hmm. Could be role propagation job failed or conditional inheritance blocked. Can you check the last role_sync job for their org?

elaine: support-bot ran a check: `support-bot: ran /job status role_sync org=acme-corp` -> latest job id 7842 FAILED with timeout, retried 3 times. (log snippet below)
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:09Z] role_sync[7842] WARN: partial apply: 14/103 bindings applied
[2026-03-10T14:12:15Z] role_sync[7842] ERROR: propagation timeout after 30s
```

jonathan: OK that matches. If the binding didn't fully apply the project-level binding may be absent even if console UI caches show membership. The console UI can reflect pending or cached state.

mike: Workaround: ask customer to remove and re-add the user to the project via the console (not SCIM) which triggers an immediate on-demand propagation, or run a manual re-apply job from ops.

elaine: Tried re-add via console -> still seeing 403. I then asked them to open console in an incognito window and relogin; UI now shows 'View' only.

jonathan: Sounds like cached session token. The service token should be unaffected by browser session, but the console UI may show stale membership. For the API token 403, need to confirm the token's scopes. Can you ask them to call `/v1/tokens/<id>` with admin creds to show token metadata?

elaine: They shared token metadata: {"id":"tk_01...","scopes":["models.read","embeddings.create"]} — no projects.* scopes. Looks like the service token got minted without the project scope graft.

mike: That suggests the token mint path didn't pick up recently-applied bindings. If token creation reads group membership at issuance time and a role_sync was partial, it won't attach project scopes. Two fixes: 1) reissue token after a successful role_sync, or 2) explicitly grant token scopes via org admin token endpoint (temporary).

jonathan: I'll kick a reapply job now: `sre-bot: /role_sync apply org=acme-corp run=true priority=high`

sre-bot: role_sync job 7848 STARTED for org=acme-corp (triggered by jonathan). Estimated time ~20s.

sre-bot: role_sync job 7848 COMPLETED. 103/103 bindings applied.

mike: Great. Elaine, please ask ACME to delete the service token and recreate it, then retry the curl. That should attach the project scopes correctly now.

elaine: Customer recreated token and retried curl -> `200 OK` and list of models returned. They confirmed console now shows Active project access after a hard refresh.

mike: Root cause: intermittent role_sync timeout during SCIM apply; tokens minted during the partial state lacked project scopes. Filed follow-up: ENG-ROLE-423 to add a pre-token-mint membership check and surface a warning in the token UI if the org's last role_sync failed.

jonathan: Also adding a short-term monitoring alert: if role_sync fails > 1 within 6 hours for an org, auto-flag new tokens from that org for manual review.

elaine: Closing the support case; customer is unblocked. Thanks all :thumbsup:
